cleared.check: Task 1 (lead L-837): the seven v3 style swaps of cycle 17 that did not reproduce, from cycles/017/own-check.work/out/stageB-own.json.mismatch.jsonl. All logs of each pool in the swap block and the block before were fetched with eth_getLogs from https://rpc.purroofgroup.com (web3_clientVersion reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31 before and after). Both pools (0x0d3e8f6949dcaca02cbd1aaf7ca840f4f36216b7 and 0x12e5f773134a6df0fcc74aedddcca0429a08eaa6) were read with eth_call and eth_getCode: factory 0x07e60782535752be279929e2dffdd136db2e6b45, 21,609 bytes of code, fee() 1100 and 2500, tick spacing 5 and 100. The code contains the 0xd78218c0 topic and not the standard Mint topic 0x7a53080b, so every mint of this factory emits the variant. v3recheck.py was rerun in this work directory with the variant read as a mint (liquidity in data word 2, ticks in topics 2 and 3).
cleared.result: All seven reproduce price, tick, liquidity and both amounts to the unit (out/own7.recheck.json: 7 ok, 2 with several steps, 2 with four calls on the 512 bit branch of mulDiv). No block before holds a log of the pool. In the five swaps that stay inside one range, parent liquidity plus the variant's liquidity equals the logged liquidity exactly (out/own7.liquidity.txt, for example 5,751,706,501,937,840 + 12,304,701,949,129,529 = 18,056,408,451,067,369 in block 50,505,119); the other two cross ticks and match through the loop. The fee these pools charge differs from fee() (800 recorded in cycle 15, 1100 now), so the fee search is the dynamic fee of this fork. Nothing is left that would point to validator arithmetic different from src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116 or SqrtPriceMath.sol.

cleared.result: 57,543 groups, 63,540 swaps, all reproduced to the unit in price, tick, liquidity and both amounts; 0 mismatches, 0 group errors (out/rest-summary.json). 17,032 swaps take several steps, 46,508 one step. 36,665 swaps make 104,643 calls on the 512 bit branch of mulDiv in their matching rerun. No call reached the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp; 17 swaps end exactly on an initialized tick boundary. 182 groups hold the Mint variant, and they are the only groups where the collector's mint and burn count differs from the live logs; the collector's swap count equals the live count in every group. Three other topics appear and change no liquidity: 0x596b5739 (CollectProtocol, 5), 0x0cba8718 (two words such as 1300 and 1200 on the dynamic fee pool 0x0d3e8f69, 212) and 0x3ac0594a (one word, pools 0x06f23b65 and 0x0139ad92, 312); every group holding them reproduces. 49,012 of the matches come from the fee search, 13,500 exact input, 1,019 exact output, 9 to limit. cleared.check: Task 3: the three plants of the script on one sample of 2,000 of the 57,543 groups (sorted(random.Random(18).sample(rest, 2000))), rerun from an RPC cache written during Task 2 so the plants see the same answers. An unplanted run of the same sample from the cache reproduces the Task 2 counts exactly (2,195 swaps ok, 1,249 with a 512 bit call).
cleared.result: Planted MULMOD (one more when the modulus is not 2^256-1 and the product needs 512 bits) breaks 405 swaps in 352 of the 1,181 groups whose unplanted match used the branch. In the other 829 groups the swap also matches a rerun with the price limit set to the logged price, which takes no 512 bit product, so about one third of the swaps counted on the branch need it to match (about 11,900 of the 36,665 in Task 2 by that ratio). Planted TickMath (getSqrtPriceAtTick one unit high at multiples of 10) breaks 130 swaps. The fallback plant breaks none, because no sampled swap reaches the fallback branch; mined swaps give no evidence for that branch. The comparison can fail on the 512 bit branch and on TickMath. The fee search, which treats the fee as free, and the limit-at-logged-price mode are the two places where it is lenient.

leads.question: Can the v3 check cover the about 1,010,000 swaps of the two factories 0xf77bd082c627aa54591cf2f2eaa811fd1ab3b1f3 and 0x5f95e92c338e6453111fc55ee66d4aafcce661a7 (for example pools 0xbe512f5881b85c48d9c17bc5bb2be047d156d696 and 0x12df9913e9e08453440e3c4b1ae73819160b513e)? Their pools revert on slot0() and answer globalState() (0xe76c01e4), so they are Algebra style and need a tick tree view and that fork's swap step.
leads.why: They are a third of HyperEVM's v3 style swaps and stay outside every check of the closed validator's arithmetic.

leads.question: For the 36,665 swaps of Task 2 that touched the 512 bit branch, how many still match when the rerun must use the open price limit (no limit at the logged price) and the fee read from the pool or from the 0x0cba8718 event in place of the fee search?
leads.why: The planted MULMOD fault showed that two thirds of the swaps counted on the branch also match without it; a strict mode would turn the 36,665 into a measured count of swaps that need the branch.

leadResults.answer: Rerun in this cycle from the saved records: all seven swaps reproduce once the 0xd78218c0 Mint variant of factory 0x07e60782 is read; no log of the pool in the block before; liquidity arithmetic closes exactly on the five single range swaps.

All 57,543 remaining m512? groups were run with the Mint variant read: 63,540 swaps reproduced, 17,032 with several steps, 36,665 with calls on the 512 bit branch (104,643 calls), 0 mismatches. Plants: MULMOD breaks 405 and TickMath 130 of 2,195 swaps; fallback has no mined instance. The two Algebra style factories were not added and are a new lead.
